sandbox3d.title: 3D Sandbox
sandbox3d.subtitle: Practice with Three.js and React Three Fiber: PBR materials, lights, shadows, and orbit controls — common in landings and product configurators.
sandbox3d.controlsHint: Drag to orbit · scroll to zoom · try shapes and materials.
sandbox3d.canvasLabelTour: Virtual tour with video and guided stops

stack.title: Quick reference
stack.subtitle: Core concepts of the 3D web stack and how they fit together.
stack.integrationIntro: Each layer delegates to the one below: React declares the scene, Three.js represents it, WebGL runs it on the GPU.

concepts.title: WebGL
concepts.body: Browser API that draws on the GPU: buffers, shaders, and the render pipeline.

concepts.title: Three.js
concepts.body: Scene graph on WebGL: Scene, Camera, Mesh, Material, and Light.

concepts.title: React Three Fiber (R3F)
concepts.body: Declarative React components over Three.js; useFrame for per-frame animation.

concepts.title: PBR
concepts.body: meshStandardMaterial with metalness/roughness; shadows via directionalLight + castShadow.

concepts.title: Performance
concepts.body: Reduce polygons, adaptive dpr, React Suspense, and code-split with ssr: false.

layers.title: Next.js (App Router)
layers.summary: Mounts Canvas client-only; avoids hydrating WebGL on the server.

layers.title: React Three Fiber
layers.summary: Canvas, hooks (useFrame, useThree), and React → Three.js reconciliation.

layers.title: @react-three/drei
layers.summary: Ready-made helpers: OrbitControls, CameraControls, PerspectiveCamera, lights, textures.

layers.title: Three.js
layers.summary: Geometries, PBR materials, lights, shadows, and VideoTexture.

layers.title: WebGL / GPU
layers.summary: Low-level pipeline that runs shaders and draws pixels to the screen.

demoMap.playground: PBR materials + useFrame (auto-rotate) + OrbitControls via drei; Canvas loaded with dynamic in Next.js.
demoMap.room: Full scene graph (walls, furniture, lights) with meshStandardMaterial, shadows, and OrbitControls.
demoMap.tour: CameraControls for stop transitions + manual VideoTexture on meshBasicMaterial.

playground.label: Materials
playground.intro: Interactive lab to explore materials and shapes in WebGL.
capabilities: Adjust color, metalness, and roughness in real time on any geometry.
Toggle wireframe and auto-rotate to review meshes and motion.
Orbit and zoom freely around the 3D object.
Embed React Three Fiber scenes in Next.js without server-side hydration.
Optimize performance with client-only Canvas, Suspense, and code-splitting.

room.label: Room
room.intro: Navigable 3D preview of a furnished bedroom in the browser.
capabilities: Walk through a full interior with orbit controls.
Show furnished spaces without static renders or on-site visits.
Simulate warm lighting, shadows, and depth in real time.
Present rooms for real estate, hospitality, or retail.
Scale to GLTF/Blender models when the client provides assets.

tour.label: Video tour
tour.intro: Virtual tour with room-to-room jumps and in-scene video.
capabilities: Guide visitors through stops (living, bedroom, kitchen) with camera transitions.
Play video on a 3D screen inside the environment.
Combine free exploration with selectable points of interest.
Replicate 360° walkthroughs and web showrooms for property marketing.
Ship embeddable tours in production-ready Next.js landings.

motionLab.title: Motion principles on scroll
motionLab.subtitle: Interactive scroll-driven demos inspired by classic UI animation techniques.
motionLab.intro: Each section explains one technique used in product UIs — easing, stagger, fade, morph, masking, depth, parallax, zoom, and horizontal slide — with a live demo you can replay as you scroll.

fade.demoText: Content fades in as it enters the viewport — best paired with position or scale.

transform.demoToggleLabel: Toggle shape morph between icon and expanded panel

slideX.scrollHint: Keep scrolling — panels move on the X axis

panels.title: Discover
panels.body: Scroll drives translateX: the viewport stays fixed while the track pans sideways.

panels.title: Compare
panels.body: Each panel enters from the right — ideal for feature tours and step-by-step stories.

panels.title: Decide
panels.body: Pair with easing and stagger so horizontal motion feels intentional, not accidental.

panels.title: Ship
panels.body: Same pattern powers Apple-style landings and editorial product pages in pure CSS + scroll.

easing.title: The basics of easing
easing.body: Objects in nature accelerate and decelerate. Easing mimics that on screen so motion feels organic instead of robotic.

offset.title: Offset and delay
offset.body: Staggering elements by a few milliseconds creates hierarchy, softness, and guides attention through the layout.

fade.title: Fade in / fade out
fade.body: Opacity transitions are the most versatile entrance technique — especially when combined with position or scale.

transform.title: Transform & morph
transform.body: Morphing one shape into another maintains continuity and keeps the eye anchored during navigation.

masking.title: Masking
masking.body: Mask reveals add softness and depth — the content feels like it unfolds inside its container.

dimension.title: Dimension
dimension.body: Layered cards at different depths make flat interfaces feel spatial and tactile.

parallax.title: Parallax
parallax.body: Layers moving at different speeds on scroll create depth and a cinematic sense of space.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.body: Scale transitions connect screens narratively and signal that more detail lives beneath the surface.

slideX.title: Horizontal slide
slideX.body: Vertical scroll can drive horizontal translation — sticky viewport, moving track. A staple for storytelling layouts and product walkthroughs.
